messages:
elaine-sales: Hey team — POC kickoff with Acme tomorrow. They insist on HSM-backed, customer-managed keys for all inference workloads. Need quick alignment on what Redwood supports for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Who can take the KMS/HSM runbook?

sam-se: I can run the tech presales. Quick summary: we support CMK via envelope encryption. For Private we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM (PKCS#11 or cloud KMS). For Hosted, we do a customer KMS grant + key-wrapping flow (we never get raw key material).

maria-customer: Our CISO (raj) will only sign off if keys are in an HSM and rotations are auditable. We use AWS CloudHSM and AWS KMS with custom key policy. BYOK preferred.

raj-ciso: Confirming: we need FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated HSM, cross-account CloudTrail logs for every Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey API call, and a documented rotation plan (90d). Also need proof that Redwood cannot export unwrapped DEKs.

nina-sec: @raj-ciso we hear you. On our side, policy is: customer-managed keys via cloud KMS or on-prem HSM for Private. For hosted customers we support an envelope-key model: customer CMK (KMS) wraps per-tenant DEKs that live encrypted in our storage. We never store plaintext keys. We can emit KMS request IDs into our audit logs.

kevin-eng: Technical notes: - For AWS: use GenerateDataKey without Plaintext (GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext) + Envelope. Actually we use GenerateDataKey then immediately discard plaintext in memory after wrapping, but we can switch to GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext + ReEncrypt pattern if they insist. - For CloudHSM: we support PKCS#11 interface in Private deploy; need network routing and KMS proxy.

sam-se: Important to flag: Hosted API cannot accept customer HSM connections directly (no inside-the-cloud HSM peering). Hosted customers must use KMS-based envelope flow (we call customer's KMS using a cross-account role/grant). Dedicated/Private can support customer HSMs via direct integration.

maria-customer: How do we rotate keys with minimal downtime? If we rotate the CMK, do you re-encrypt all stored DEKs? That could be heavy for our dataset size.

nina-sec: Two options: 1) rewrap-on-access (lazy rewrap): keep existing wrapped DEKs until first use after rotation, then rewrap with new CMK — zero downtime, gradual cost. 2) bulk rewrap job: run a background re-encryption job that rewraps all DEKs immediately — takes time but gives clean state. We recommend lazy rewrap for large stores, bulk for small controlled datasets. We'll document both.

kevin-eng: Implementation detail: we store encryption metadata: {key_alias, wrap_version, kms_key_id, wrapped_key_blob}. Rewrap just updates wrapped_key_blob and wrap_version. No token data is re-encrypted, just the DEK wrapper.

raj-ciso: We also need HSM attestation, key origin proof (i.e., key material generated in HSM), and a rotation policy that preserves key provenance. Can Redwood provide attestation artifacts or integration to pull AWS KMS key metadata?

nina-sec: Yes — for Cloud KMS we can surface KMS key metadata (ARN, origin: AWS_KMS/EXTERNAL, creation date, keyState). For customer-hosted HSMs we require the customer to provide attestation statements; on Private deployments we can validate local HSM attestation during onboarding.

sam-se: Action items for POC: 1) send our KMS integration doc to Acme (we have a template). 2) SE to demo envelope flow with GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext. 3) Security to confirm logs mapping to customer SIEM (CloudTrail -> S3 -> SIEM). 4) Engineering to outline rewrap options and a rough timeline/cost.

elaine-sales: Assigning: sam (SE) to demo, kevin (eng) to write rewrap doc, nina (sec) to provide attestation checklist. I'll update Acme and loop raj. Needed by EOD today for kickoff deck.

kevin-eng: I'll draft the rewrap + rotation playbook. Also note a blocker: cross-account KMS grants require customer to add our AWS principal to their key policy. Some legal teams balk at granting long-lived permissions; we can limit to time-bound grants and use short-lived roles.

raj-ciso: Time-bound grants are acceptable. Also need assurance on key usage restrictions (only Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey, no ScheduleKeyDeletion).

nina-sec: We can add a few guardrails: - Minimum: grants limited to kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:ReEncrypt* - Audit-only: cloudtrail + signed request IDs returned in API responses - No key export: confirm we never call ExportKeyMaterial for EXTERNAL keys.

sam-se: Quick snippet to include in the POC deck (AWS grant example):
```
{
  "Sid": "RedwoodKmsAccess",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDDENW:role/redwood-kms-role"},
  "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:ReEncrypt*"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```

maria-customer: That looks fine. One last ask: can we get a short ops runbook showing steps if a key is compromised (revoke, rotation, replay prevention)?

nina-sec: Yes — runbook outline: 1) disable CMK (set key state to PendingDisable/Disabled) 2) issue new CMK and run rewrap (bulk or lazy) 3) rotate DEKs and revoke old grants 4) verify audit trail and CIEM alerts. We'll attach exact CLI commands for AWS and CloudHSM in the doc.

deploy-bot: Attached: https://internal.redwood/docs/kms-hsm-integration — includes sample grant JSON, rewrap scripts, and Private deployment checklist.

elaine-sales: Perfect. I'll share these with Acme and schedule demo. Thanks everyone — please drop any last-minute blockers here. :thumbsup:

sam-se: One potential enterprise blocker: some procurement teams require customer-managed HSM for Hosted products — we should clarify in contract language we only support BYOK via KMS grants for hosted and HSM direct only for Private. I'll add an FAQ slide.

kevin-eng: Also flag network: Private HSM integrations need VPN/DirectConnect + firewall rules for PKCS#11 endpoint. Add to onboarding checklist.

nina-sec: No other blockers from security. We'll finalize attestation checklist and rotation playbook by EOD.

maria-customer: Thanks — Raj and I will review docs once you send.

elaine-sales: Closing the loop: will post the kickoff deck and invite the team.
